graph.description: Graph name; optional when the key or server has a default.

tools.name: graphs
tools.description: The graphs on this server: list them (default action; shows which one the other tools use when you pass no `graph`), or create one with action "create" and a `name` (lowercase letters, digits, - and _). Every other tool works on one graph.

name.description: For create: the new graph's name.

policies.description: For create, optional: require_evidence (enforce | warn | off; default enforce), inline_text_limit, normalize_types.

tools.name: overview
tools.description: What the graph holds: counts, node and link types in use, evidence kinds, policies, recent batches, naming conventions. Call first. With `type`, details of one node or link type (property keys and fill rates, link patterns, examples).

type.description: A node type or link type to describe.

tools.name: search
tools.description: Ranked search over node names and aliases (exact, prefix, fuzzy) and full text of nodes, links and evidence.

types.description: Only these node or link types.

tools.name: resolve
tools.description: Does this already exist? For up to 100 described entities, existing matching nodes with scores and a verdict (match, ambiguous, none). Use before writing new nodes.

hints.description: Property values that should agree, e.g. {"born": {"$date": "1815"}}.

tools.name: get
tools.description: Fetch nodes, links, evidence or citations by ID, key or {type, name}: fields, links of a node, support counts, citing evidence, evidence content.

include.description: links {limit, types} | false, support bool, evidence {limit} | false, content true | {from, max_chars}.

tools.name: write
tools.description: One atomic, idempotent batch: evidence, nodes, links, citations and updates. Give each item a `ref` ("@x") to refer to it within the batch; facts cite evidence with `cite: ["@src"]`. Matching nodes are reused, not duplicated.

evidence.description: {ref, kind: text|url|file|image|document|observation|…, content, uri, title, parent, source_date, author, …}

nodes.description: {ref, type, name, aliases, labels, summary, props, key, create_new, cite}

links.description: {ref, type, from, to, directed, props, valid_from, valid_to, cite}

tools.name: retract
tools.description: Soft-delete (retract) or restore objects, or everything a batch created. Cascades to dependent links and citations; nothing is lost.

tools.name: merge
tools.description: Merge duplicate nodes into one; links, citations, aliases and properties move to the surviving node and old IDs keep resolving.

tools.name: neighbors
tools.description: Subgraph around start nodes: k hops (depth or per-hop steps) with link-type, direction and node-type filters.

tools.name: paths
tools.description: How two nodes connect: shortest, all shortest or k shortest paths, with the evidence count of each link.

tools.name: find
tools.description: Structured query without a query language: filter by field conditions, group by expressions, aggregate (count, count_distinct, sum, avg, min, max, median), sort and page. Fields: id, type, name, status, prop:<key>, degree(TYPE), dates with .year/.decade, …

where.description: {field, op, value} or {all|any: [...]}, {not: …}, {linked: {link_type, direction, node}}. Ops: eq ne lt lte gt gte between in not_in exists missing contains starts_with.

tools.name: history
tools.description: Change history of one object (newest first), or every change after a sequence number (oldest first) to catch up.

tools.name: stats
tools.description: Base statistics of the graph: counts by status and type, degree distribution and top hubs, growth per day, evidence by kind and web domain, uncited and most-cited evidence. Use it to judge how large, connected and well sourced a graph is.
